title: JavaScript Debugging Applied Check
description: Test your ability to diagnose practical JavaScript bugs using DevTools, stack traces, async reasoning, network evidence, DOM inspection, and tests.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: Check whether `button` is `null` and whether the listener setup code runs
Change every `const` to `var`
Add `mode: "no-cors"`
Remove all CSS from the page

questions.explanation: If the selector does not find an element or setup code never runs, the listener will not be attached.

options.text: `fetch()` was not awaited, so `response` is a Promise
`response.json()` can never be awaited
The function cannot be marked `async`
The URL must be uppercase

questions.explanation: `fetch()` returns a Promise. The code must use `const response = await fetch(...)` before calling `response.json()`.

questions.prompt: A form briefly logs the right data, then the page reloads and the log disappears. What should you check?

options.text: Whether the submit handler calls `event.preventDefault()`
Whether the array uses `.map()`
Whether `console.table()` is installed
Whether the status code is exactly 201

questions.explanation: Forms submit and navigate by default. `event.preventDefault()` is commonly needed for JavaScript-handled forms.

questions.prompt: A request appears in the Network panel with status `401`. What should you inspect first?

options.text: Authentication details such as token, cookies, credentials, or authorization header
Only the element's `z-index`
Whether a loop uses `break`
Whether the JavaScript file has comments

questions.explanation: `401` means the request is not authenticated, so inspect auth-related request details.

options.text: Check whether the async requests can finish out of order and track the latest request
Assume the browser always runs requests in call order
Remove every `await`
Use `JSON.stringify()` on the button element

questions.explanation: This is likely a race condition. Later requests can finish before earlier requests.

questions.prompt: A stack trace points to `calculateTotal`, but that function received `cart` as `undefined`. What should you do next?

options.text: Use the call stack to find who called it and where `cart` came from
Immediately return `0` for every error without investigation
Rename the function until the error disappears
Ignore the stack trace because it is never useful

questions.explanation: The crash happens in `calculateTotal`, but the root cause may be an earlier caller passing the wrong value.

questions.prompt:
Which debugging approach best narrows this flow?
```text
form input -> request payload -> API response -> transform -> render
```

options.text: Inspect a middle step, then decide whether the bug is before or after it
Change all steps at once
Only inspect the final rendered text
Delete the request payload

questions.explanation: Binary search debugging checks the middle of a flow to narrow which half contains the bug.

options.text: It repeatedly reparses and rewrites the body instead of batching the DOM update
Template literals cannot be used in loops
`for...of` cannot read arrays
`innerHTML` always throws a SyntaxError

questions.explanation: Repeated DOM writes can be expensive. Building the HTML once and inserting it once is usually better.

questions.prompt: A search API is called on every keystroke and the UI feels sluggish. Which technique is likely appropriate?

options.text: Debounce the input handler so work runs after the user pauses typing
Call the API twice per keystroke
Store the password in the console
Turn the input into a `var`

questions.explanation: Debouncing reduces repeated work caused by rapid events such as input changes.

questions.prompt: What is the best next step after you fix a reproducible bug?

options.text: Rerun the reproduction steps and add a focused test when possible
Leave temporary `debugger` statements in the code
Remove the error message without testing
Assume all related cases are fixed automatically

questions.explanation: Verifying the original steps and adding a test helps prove the fix and prevent regressions.

questions.prompt:
Which fix addresses the cause instead of only hiding the symptom?
```js
const discount = total * coupon.percent; // NaN when coupon.percent is "20%"
```

options.text: Parse and validate percentage strings before calculating
Use `total * coupon.percent || 0` everywhere without checking input
Delete the coupon object
Log `NaN` as a success message

questions.explanation: Parsing and validating the input fixes the invalid value. A fallback may hide the bug without correcting the cause.

questions.prompt: A removed DOM element still seems to consume memory because it is stored in a global array. What is the likely issue?

options.text: A lingering reference prevents the removed element from being garbage collected
DOM elements cannot be removed from memory
The element needs a different CSS color
The array should be converted to a string

questions.explanation: Objects can stay in memory while reachable from references such as global arrays, caches, closures, or listeners.
